{{nihongo|'''Arima Shrine'''|有間神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Arino-chō, Kita Ward, Kobe City, Hyōgo Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking}} it was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. Its shrine crest is the “{{ill|Tomoe|Q1557435|qid=Q1557435|lt=triple tomoe}}.” {{nihongo|'''Arima Shrine'''|有間神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Ōkami}}''' (おおなむちのおおかみ)
* '''{{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Ōkami}}''' (すくなひこなのおおかみ)
* '''{{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|Q2842779|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Ōkami}}''' (あめのみなかぬしのおおかみ) – Enshrined in {{ill|969|Q23708|qid=Q23708}} (1st year of {{ill|Anna (era)|Q1373003|qid=Q1373003}}).
* '''{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Ōkami}}''' (ことしろぬしのおおかみ) – Enshrined in {{ill|1935|Q18658|qid=Q18658}} (10th year of {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}) from {{ill|Miho Shrine|Q3313076|qid=Q3313076}}.

== Name ==
The origin of the shrine’s name is unclear, but “Arima” is considered an older spelling of “Arima.” According to the history of Arino Village, “ari” means mountain, and “arima” refers to an open place among mountains. It is also unclear when the place-name “Arima” came to be written as such. Because the shrine was once located in Sannō Valley before its relocation, it is said to have formerly been called '''Sannō-gū'''.

== History ==
In ancient times, the shrine was enshrined in Sannō Valley of Narae Village in Yamaguchi Manor (Arima District). The date of foundation is unknown, but according to shrine tradition, the earliest record is that {{ill|Emperor Jomei|Q329761|qid=Q329761}} visited and worshiped here in September {{ill|631|Q31577|qid=Q31577}} (3rd year of Emperor Shōmu) when he traveled to {{ill|Arima Onsen|Q4790673|qid=Q4790673}}. It is believed that the shrine existed even before that.

In {{ill|715|Q23528|qid=Q23528}} (1st year of {{ill|Reiki (era)|Q1373115|qid=Q1373115}}), a massive flood from {{ill|Mount Rokkō|Q462120|qid=Q462120}} caused the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Arima River}} to overflow, washing away the shrine buildings. By divine oracle, the shrine was relocated to Nishio Village in {{ill|Arino|Q18700240|qid=Q18700240|lt=Arino Manor}}. A temporary shrine was established until construction was completed; the place where the sacred object was temporarily enshrined later became {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tao Shrine}}. Additionally, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Okaba Wakamiya Shrine}} was built at the site that served as the temporary resting place (otabisho) during the relocation.

During the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} era, when the {{ill|Siege of Miki|Q11242477|qid=Q11242477}} occurred, the shrine buildings were damaged by warfare because the shrine priest, of the {{ill|Takeda clan|ar|عشيرة تاكيدا|ca|Clan Takeda|cs|Klan Takeda|de|Takeda (Klan)|eo|Takeda (klano)|es|Clan Takeda|eu|Takeda klana|fa|خاندان تاکدا|fr|Clan Takeda|glk|تاكدا كوگا|hu|Takeda-ház|id|Klan Takeda|it|Clan Takeda|ja|武田氏|ko|다케다씨|mk|Такеда (клан)|nl|Takeda (familie)|no|Takeda-klanen|pl|Takeda (ród)|pt|Clã Takeda|ru|Такэда|sr|Клан Такеда|th|ตระกูลทาเกดะ|tr|Takeda boyu|uk|Рід Такеда|zh|武田氏|qid=Q1210114}}, was related by marriage to the {{ill|Bessho clan|Q2975222|qid=Q2975222}}, lords of {{ill|Miki Castle|Q11242473|qid=Q11242473}}.

In the Edo period, the shrine received donations from the lords of the {{ill|Sanda Domain|Q10863363|qid=Q10863363}} such as {{ill|Kuki Takakuni|Q11370504|qid=Q11370504}}, and later from the {{ill|Okabe Domain|Q10863332|qid=Q10863332}} of {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398|lt=Bushū}}, who became local rulers. Until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535|lt=separation of Shinto and Buddhism}}, the adjacent “Sannōzan Jingū-ji” stood nearby, and the shrine was known as Sannō Gongen. The former temple site is now a parking lot, and the statue of {{ill|Acala|Q337624|qid=Q337624}} that stood within the precincts is enshrined as a subsidiary shrine.

As the general guardian shrine of {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}}’s {{ill|Arima district|Q11516836|qid=Q11516836}}, it attracted widespread devotion. Because the old name Sannō-gū is associated with “ubuno-o” (the umbilical cord), it was worshiped as a deity of safe childbirth. At the otabisho there is a “Koyasu Stone,” where pregnant women prayed for safe delivery, and after childbirth, mother and child were said to purify themselves in the river flowing before the shrine. It is also said that prayers were offered at the shrine for the healthy growth of newborns, and thus the shrine is revered as a guardian of children.

The shrine grove (chinju no mori) covers approximately 28,000 square meters and has been selected as one of the {{ill|Hyōgo’s 100 Selected Forests|Q11276623|qid=Q11276623}}. Of this, about 7,000 square meters of a grove of {{ill|Castanopsis|Q1065400|qid=Q1065400|lt=shii}} trees has been designated both as an environmental green conservation area by Hyōgo Prefecture and as a natural monument by Kobe City.

* {{ill|1869|Q7720|qid=Q7720}} (2nd year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}) – The shrine temple is abolished due to the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535|lt=separation of Shinto and Buddhism}}.

* {{ill|2011|Q1994|qid=Q1994}} (Heisei 23) {{ill|June 7|Q2616|qid=Q2616}} – The shrine office is completely destroyed by fire.
* {{ill|2012|Q1990|qid=Q1990}} (Heisei 24) {{ill|June 24|Q2665|qid=Q2665}} – The shrine office is rebuilt.
* {{ill|2015|Q2002|qid=Q2002}} (Heisei 27) – Marks the 1,300th anniversary of the relocation.

== Shrine buildings ==
== Main hall and worship hall ==
The current {{ill|Shinto architecture|Q3080012|qid=Q3080012|lt=honden}} was rebuilt in 1796 and is of the {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684|lt=three-bay nagare-zukuri}} style. Formerly only the main hall and {{ill|Shinto architecture|Q3080012|qid=Q3080012|lt=heiden}} existed, but after World War II a reinforced-concrete {{ill|Shinto architecture|Q3080012|qid=Q3080012|lt=haiden}} was newly constructed.

The kuroki torii standing before the worship hall was originally used for {{ill|Emperor Kōmei|Q299179|qid=Q299179}}’s {{ill|Daijosai|Q11433653|qid=Q11433653}} and was bestowed in {{ill|1849|Q7650|qid=Q7650}}; after it decayed, it was rebuilt in concrete.
